standard.title: SPECIFICATION FOR 4-METRE LEVELLING STAFF (TELESCOPIC)
standard.sector: Optical and Mathematical Instruments Sectional Committee, EDC 36 / Surveying Instruments Subcommittee, EDC 36 : 3

sectional_committee.name: Optical and Mathematical Instruments Sectional Committee

standard.description: This standard prescribes the requirements for the 4-m telescopic levelling staff, which is a mechanical device used in tertiary levelling to provide height control for topographical or engineering surveys [1, 2].
standard.scope: This standard prescribes the requirements for the 4-m telescopic levelling staff, which is a mechanical device used in tertiary levelling to provide height control for topographical or engineering surveys [1, 2].

certification.description: Conformity assessment and licensing are supported by the Bureau of Indian Standards Certification Marking scheme, with compliance systems administered directly by BIS [1].
requirements: The staff must consist of three distinct sliding sections. Design tolerances must ensure the top section slides smoothly into the middle section, and the middle section slides into the bottom section [1].

The staff must be manufactured from one of the following approved seasoned timbers: Teak (Tectona grandis Linn. f.), Cypress (Cupressus torulosa Don.), Kail (Pinus wallichiana A.B. Jacks.), Deodar (Cedrus deodara Loudon), Aini (Artocarpus hirsuta Lamk.), Champ (Michelia sp.), or Hollock (Terminalia myriocarpa) [3].

The selected timber must be thoroughly seasoned, radially sawn, and completely free from physical defects like knots, cracks, shakes, insect attack, and decay. The moisture content must be strictly maintained within the range of 8 to 12 percent [3].
The nomenclature, dimensions, and profiles of different assembly parts (including the shoe, bottom cap, middle cap, and top) must conform precisely to Figures 1 to 9 of the standard [2].
Any observed or calculated test value expressing the result of a test must be rounded off to the same number of significant places as the specified value, in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 [2].
